correctness.rationale: The parity obstruction handles all even m. For odd m the base norm-two solution yields an integral norm-one multiplier; powers give exact integral norm-two solutions. For p|m, x²≡2 mod p forces p≥7 and p∤x. In the binomial formula the first term has valuation v_p(y)+v_p(n), and all later terms strictly exceed it because v_p(2j+1)<j≤jv_p(m). Thus v_p(Y_n)=v_p(y)+v_p(n); n=m^r supplies all odd-power coefficients and fixed-r infinite families. Converse substitution and the m=7,23 minimality check are exact. A standalone verifier independently checks 39 cases, without replacing the proof.

value.rationale: Van Doorn specifically motivates identifying squarefree multipliers for his cubic Pell powerful-number construction. An explicit equivalence with the base coefficient, valid at all odd-power levels and supported by an exact local valuation law, reduces this natural family of Diophantine tests and generates new infinite powerful-AP examples, including the next minimal squarefree multiplier 23. The theorem is structural, not an arbitrary finite census; it makes no unsupported claim about consecutive powerful terms.
